quotes.text: Radar doesn’t support deprecated payment methods.
Users on Radar Standard or above are protected by a set of default risk controls that block high-risk payments.
Stripe might still block payments for a variety of reasons, including but not limited to fraud risk, sanctions, and other compliance and regulatory considerations.
You can adjust individual payment method rules with the `:payment_method_type:` attribute.

findings: November describes broad default Radar protection for all Stripe users and supported methods, excludes deprecated methods, limits the default high-risk blocking controls to Radar Standard and higher, and says Stripe may still block Lite traffic for fraud, sanctions or other considerations.

Custom risk settings depend on plan. November names broad method families including cards, wallets, bank debits/redirects/transfers, BNPL, real-time payments, stablecoins and vouchers. May instead provides method-level status rows and preview opt-in for Fraud Teams/Platforms users.

Both captures describe enabled rules and settings carrying over by default to supported payment methods, and merchant targeting via the payment_method_type attribute, illustrated with a Bacs Direct Debit condition. Existing controls include lists, custom rules, backtesting and analytics within plan scope.
substantive_changes: November narrows the stated default high-risk-controls scope to Standard+ and explicitly retains possible blocking for Lite users. It qualifies scope to supported, non-deprecated payment methods.

November changes the custom settings documentation from old plan names and method-level full/private-preview status listings to plan eligibility and broad family routes, adds distinct families such as bank redirects/transfers, real-time payments and vouchers, and omits the old preview opt-in wording. This changes documented scope and presentation without demonstrating a particular preview graduated or an opt-in was removed.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May 10, 2026 capture as the authority for its all-user wording, Fraud Teams/Platforms framing, named method-level supported and preview statuses, most-preview screening and preview opt-in instructions. Keep shared individual-rule targeting and list, rule, analytics and backtesting workflows with correct plan scope.
conflicts: The current summary markets high-risk blocking to every Radar user and lists stale custom-method statuses without a capture date. Preserve May wording as historical and replace undated assertions with November Standard+, Lite may still be blocked, and explicit plan and method qualifications.

A separately captured November How Radar works matrix marks all-payment-methods fraud prevention unsupported for Lite, while this page says default protection is active broadly. Keep the general default description, no all-methods feature claim for Lite, Standard+ default controls, and individual Stripe blocking distinct. The matrix separately documents Plus/Pro eligibility for transaction custom rules/backtesting/custom list capabilities (raw/stripe-radar-how-radar-works-2026-11-07.md:26-44).

The Radar concept's coverage paragraph already reflects November's Standard+/Lite and plan difference, but its source-list entry still presents May cards/ACH/SEPA support and BNPL/wallets/stablecoin preview as undated. Update its source locator label to describe both captures.

Both assigned captures illustrate bacs_debit in the payment_method_type predicate (old raw lines 44-48, new raw lines 41-45). The separately linked Supported Attributes capture on each date gives the supported values as card, sepa_debit and us_bank_account, omitting bacs_debit (raw/stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes-2026.md:166 and raw/stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes-2026-11-07.md:170). Preserve the Bacs example alongside the exact conflict and route to source-stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes.
unresolved_questions: The November families do not establish the new eligibility or preview state of any individual method previously marked private preview, including Bacs. Its preserved Bacs rule example cannot resolve enrollment status. The missing May preview opt-in text does not settle the fate of that requirement.
The Bacs example and supported-value rows leave runtime rule acceptance for bacs_debit unresolved independently of Bacs entitlement.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/supported-payment-methods, November 7, 2026 says Stripe enables Radar fraud protection by default for all Stripe users and supported methods, excluding deprecated methods. Standard and above have default controls that block high-risk payments. Stripe can still block Lite payments for fraud, sanctions and other reasons. Merchants can see blocked payments on the Radar risk controls page (new raw lines 7-13). May 10, 2026 stated protection by default for all users and high-risk-blocking default controls for all Radar users, said most preview methods were supported, and excluded deprecated methods (old raw lines 6-14). November conditions merchant custom risk settings on a supporting plan and describes cards, wallet, bank debit/redirect/transfer, BNPL, real-time, stablecoin and voucher families (new raw lines 15-37). May names Fraud Teams/Platforms and gives an individual payment method matrix with supported rows and named private previews requiring opt-in (old raw lines 16-40). Supported methods inherit active rules/settings. Eligible merchants can target individual methods with payment_method_type, illustrated by Bacs Direct Debit, with no evidence of particular merchant eligibility or example execution (new raw lines 39-45, old raw lines 42-48). source-stripe-radar-supported-payment-methods currently summarizes May's coverage without the dated boundary and omits November's plan-specific controls and Lite caveat.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/supported-payment-methods, update source-stripe-radar-supported-payment-methods while keeping May 10, 2026 and November 7, 2026 as factual captures. The substantive change is the documented high-risk default-control boundary at Standard and above, with possible distinct blocking on Lite. A separate November overview matrix marks all-payment-method fraud prevention unsupported on Lite, while essential card prevention is listed for Lite. Preserve both documentary scopes, with the overview providing plan rows for custom transaction rules and backtesting (new raw lines 9-17, old raw lines 8-18). Replace the current undated May table with dated May supported/private-preview/opt-in status detail and November plan-dependent method families. The changed table-to-list format is presentational, but losing named statuses and adding broad categories affects what the capture can answer. The linked destinations are navigation, including two wallet labels sharing the same anchor, and do not establish particular eligibility, GA or the end of opt-in for previously private-preview methods (new raw lines 19-37, old raw lines 20-40 and old raw line 50). Preserve the inherited rules and method targeting example (new raw lines 39-45, old raw lines 42-48), keep the reciprocal stripe-radar and Radar overview routes plus the linked risk-settings route, and date the concept's currently undated preview source label. Keep the Bacs Direct Debit predicate example from both supported-method captures (old raw lines 44-48, new raw lines 41-45) with the exact documentary conflict. The separate May and November Supported Attributes rows enumerate card, sepa_debit and us_bank_account, omitting bacs_debit (raw/stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes-2026.md:166 and raw/stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes-2026-11-07.md:170). Route to source-stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes for those dated rows. Runtime acceptance of that predicate and account entitlement for Bacs remain unresolved.
